results.corrected_title: METR Q4 2026 update: time horizons double about every 3.6 months, and AI R&D acceleration cannot be ruled out
results.corrected_summary: METR's Q4 2026 capability update, published 20 November, estimates that the 50% time horizon across the combined TH1.1 and TH2 suites doubles roughly every 3.61 months (95% CI 2.08-4.94). The TH2 verifiable subset shows a faster doubling of about 1.65 months, but METR calls this result noisy. Models usually match or beat skilled humans on tasks with strong feedback signals, but do worse on tasks that are costlier to verify. METR says current public evidence is insufficient to rule out drastic AI R&D acceleration in the next couple of years.
key_facts: Combined TH1.1 and TH2 50% time horizon doubling time is about 3.61 months, 95% CI 2.08-4.94
The 1.65-month figure applies to the TH2 verifiable subset; METR says it is noisy
On the three tasks with formal human baselines, the best model outperformed every human baseliner
On Budget NanoGPT, top human speedrunners still achieved much larger speedups than the AI agents
METR: current public evidence is insufficient to rule out drastic AI R&D acceleration in the next couple of years

results.corrected_title: Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot Workspaces and Autopilot announced, rolling out via Frontier
results.corrected_summary: At Ignite 2026, which runs 17-20 November, Microsoft presented Copilot Workspaces, a shared space where people and agents work with common context. It also presented Autopilot, a persistent, proactive agent. Both are rolling out through the Frontier early-access program and are not generally available.
key_facts: Ignite 2026 runs 17-20 November, keynote coverage dated 17 November
Copilot Workspaces is a shared space for humans and agents, rolling out to Frontier
Autopilot is a persistent, proactive agent, rolling out to Frontier customers
No general availability dates or pricing confirmed
results.issues: No primary Microsoft page; Windows Blog does not mention these features.

results.corrected_title: US 'jobless growth': strong GDP and AI investment but weak hiring and a record-low labour share
results.corrected_summary: Fortune reports that US Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate while hiring stayed weak, averaging about 48,000 jobs a month over the 12 months to September. October added 165,000 jobs. Goldman Sachs says AI spending drove more than half of business-investment growth in the first three quarters of 2026. The labour share of income was 53.0% in Q3, the lowest since the series began in 1947.
key_facts: Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate
Jobs averaged about 48,000 a month over the 12 months through September; October added 165,000
Goldman Sachs: AI spending drove more than half of business-investment growth in first three quarters of 2026
Labour share was 53.0% in Q3, lowest since 1947
In October, unemployment was 7.5% for ages 20-24 against 4.1% overall

results.corrected_title: Gemini app for Mac gets computer use
results.corrected_summary: On 19 November Google added computer use to the Gemini desktop app for macOS. It can navigate native Mac apps and the web in the background, showing a live preview in the chat. Users can pause, stop or approve actions. It is English-only, US-only, and requires Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra.
key_facts: Works across native Mac apps, the web and local files
Progress shown in live preview; user can pause, stop or approve actions
English only, US only, requires Google AI Plus, Pro or Ultra
